What's actually wrong
Three real bugs, one latent:

coqc doesn't exist in that image. The rocq/rocq-prover Dockerfile installs rocq-runtime, rocq-core, coqide-server, rocq-stdlib — and explicitly skips coq-core/coq with the comment that they're transitional packages. Rocq 9.0 renamed the tools: coqc f.v → rocq compile f.v (also coqtop→rocq repl, coqdep→rocq dep, coq_makefile→rocq makefile).
The PATH loop is pointless. The image's ENTRYPOINT is opam exec --, so the opam switch is already on PATH — your own error message proves it (the opam bin dir appears twice, once from the image, once from your loop).
run_podman.sh used $(pwd), which is why it broke when you ran it from ~/src/dotnet/myrestaurant.
Latent: rootless podman maps your UID to container root, while the image runs as user rocq (uid 1000). Once rocq compile was found, it would have failed writing hello.vo into the read-only-to-it bind mount. Fixed below by compiling a scratch copy inside the container.
I collapsed run_podman.sh + verify.sh into one script that re-execs itself in the container. git rm run_podman.sh — it's gone.

verify.sh
bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# verify.sh — machine-check every Rocq (.v) file in this repository.
#
#   ./verify.sh              run the checks inside the official Rocq container
#                            (podman if present, else docker)
#   ./verify.sh --no-pull    reuse the image already on disk, skip the pull
#   ./verify.sh --native     use the rocq / coqc already installed on $PATH
#
# CI runs the exact same command, so your laptop and the GitHub runner execute
# byte-for-byte identical steps.
#
# Overrides: ROCQ_IMAGE=...   CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman|docker
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

SELF="$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
REPO_ROOT="$(dirname "$SELF")"
SELF_NAME="$(basename "$SELF")"

IMAGE="${ROCQ_IMAGE:-docker.io/rocq/rocq-prover:latest}"
NATIVE=0
PULL=1

for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --native)   NATIVE=1 ;;
        --no-pull)  PULL=0 ;;
        -h|--help)  awk 'NR>1 && /^#/ {sub(/^# ?/,""); print; next} NR>1 {exit}' "$SELF"; exit 0 ;;
        *)          echo "verify.sh: unknown option '$arg' (try --help)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

BUILD_DIR=""
cleanup() { if [[ -n "$BUILD_DIR" ]]; then rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR"; fi; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The actual verification. Runs natively, or inside the container (same code).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_checks() {
    local compiler
    if command -v rocq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        compiler=rocq            # Rocq >= 9.0 : `rocq compile foo.v`
    elif command -v coqc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        compiler=coqc            # Coq  <= 8.20: `coqc foo.v`
    else
        echo "verify.sh: neither 'rocq' nor 'coqc' is on \$PATH" >&2
        echo "           PATH=$PATH" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    local -a sources=()
    local src rel
    while IFS= read -r -d '' src; do
        sources+=("${src#"$REPO_ROOT"/}")
    done < <(find "$REPO_ROOT" -type f -name '*.v' -not -path '*/.git/*' -print0 | sort -z)

    if (( ${#sources[@]} == 0 )); then
        echo "verify.sh: no .v files found under $REPO_ROOT" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    echo "========================================="
    echo " Rocq proof verification"
    echo " compiler : $("$compiler" --version 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
    echo " sources  : ${#sources[@]} file(s) under $REPO_ROOT"
    echo "========================================="

    # Compile a scratch copy rather than the worktree itself: the repo is
    # mounted read-only in the container (a rootless container cannot write
    # there anyway), and this keeps .vo/.glob/.aux droppings out of your repo.
    BUILD_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
    for rel in "${sources[@]}"; do
        mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR/$(dirname "$rel")"
        cp "$REPO_ROOT/$rel" "$BUILD_DIR/$rel"
    done
    [[ -f "$REPO_ROOT/_CoqProject" ]] && cp "$REPO_ROOT/_CoqProject" "$BUILD_DIR/"

    cd "$BUILD_DIR"
    for rel in "${sources[@]}"; do
        echo "  -> $rel"
        if [[ $compiler == rocq ]]; then
            rocq compile "$rel"
        else
            coqc "$rel"
        fi
    done

    echo "========================================="
    echo " Success: all proofs verified"
    echo "========================================="
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Re-run this same script inside the official Rocq image.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_in_container() {
    local engine="${CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
    if [[ -z "$engine" ]]; then
        if   command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then engine=podman
        elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then engine=docker
        else
            echo "verify.sh: no podman or docker found." >&2
            echo "           Install one, or run '$SELF --native'." >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    fi

    if (( PULL )); then
        echo "Pulling $IMAGE with $engine ..."
        "$engine" pull "$IMAGE"
    fi

    # The image's ENTRYPOINT is `opam exec --`, so the opam switch (and the
    # rocq binary) is already on PATH. Nothing to set up by hand.
    exec "$engine" run --rm \
        --security-opt label=disable \
        -e ROCQ_IN_CONTAINER=1 \
        -v "$REPO_ROOT":/workspace:ro \
        -w /workspace \
        "$IMAGE" \
        bash "/workspace/$SELF_NAME"
}

if (( NATIVE )) || [[ "${ROCQ_IN_CONTAINER:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
    run_checks
else
    run_in_container
fi
.github/workflows/ci.yml
yaml
name: Rocq Proof Verification

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # ubuntu-latest ships both podman and docker; verify.sh prefers podman.
    # If podman ever misbehaves on the runner, uncomment the next two lines.
    # env:
    #   CONTAINER_ENGINE: docker
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Verify proofs
        run: bash verify.sh
actions/checkout@v7 is current (v7.0.1, July 2026), so that line was fine.

Proof.

README.md
markdown
# Rocq "Hello World" Proof Verification

A minimal, automated project that machine-checks a formal proof with the
[Rocq Prover](https://rocq-prover.org/) (formerly Coq) on every push.

The proposition proved is commutativity of conjunction: $A \land B \implies B \land A$.

---

## Project structure

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `hello.v` | The Rocq source: the proposition and its proof. |
| `verify.sh` | The whole build. Runs the checks inside the official Rocq container, or natively with `--native`. |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Checkout, then `bash verify.sh`. That's it. |
| `export.sh` | Unrelated helper: dumps the repo to `docs/llm/dump.txt` for LLM context. |

CI runs the same script you run locally, so there is no second copy of the
build logic to keep in sync.

---

## Running it

```bash
./verify.sh              # pull the latest Rocq image and verify (podman, else docker)
./verify.sh --no-pull    # reuse the image already on disk
./verify.sh --native     # use the rocq (or coqc) already installed on your PATH
./verify.sh --help
```

The script resolves its own location, so it works from any working directory.

Useful overrides:

```bash
ROCQ_IMAGE=docker.io/rocq/rocq-prover:9.2 ./verify.sh   # pin a version
CONTAINER_ENGINE=docker ./verify.sh                     # force an engine
```

Sources are copied into a scratch directory before compiling, so `.vo`,
`.glob` and `.aux` files never land in your worktree.

### Poking around interactively

```bash
podman run --rm -it \
  --security-opt label=disable \
  --userns=keep-id \
  -v "$PWD":/work -w /work \
  docker.io/rocq/rocq-prover:latest bash
```

`--userns=keep-id` maps your host UID onto the container's `rocq` user so you
can actually write files in `/work`. Inside, use `rocq compile hello.v` or
`rocq repl`.

---

## A note on `coqc` vs `rocq compile`

Rocq 9.0 renamed the command-line tools. The `rocq/rocq-prover` images install
`rocq-core` but deliberately skip the transitional `coq-core` package, so
**there is no `coqc` binary in the image**:

| Coq ≤ 8.20 | Rocq ≥ 9.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `coqc f.v` | `rocq compile f.v` |
| `coqtop` | `rocq repl` |
| `coqdep` | `rocq dep` |
| `coq_makefile` | `rocq makefile` |
| `coqchk` | `rocq check` |

`verify.sh` prefers `rocq` and falls back to `coqc`, so it also works against
an older native Coq install.

The image's `ENTRYPOINT` is `opam exec --`, which already puts the opam switch
on `PATH` — no manual `PATH` surgery is needed.

---

## Scaling past one file

`verify.sh` compiles every `.v` file it finds, in alphabetical order. Once
files start depending on each other, add a `_CoqProject` and switch the loop to
`rocq makefile -f _CoqProject -o Makefile.coq && make -f Makefile.coq`.

---

## AI disclosure

Built in collaboration with Gemini (Google AI) for the original Coq proof and
CI scaffolding, and Claude (Anthropic) for the migration to the Rocq 9.x
toolchain and the single-entry-point build script.
Latest stable Rocq is 9.2.0 (9.3-rc1 is out), so :latest gets you 9.2.x. If you want CI to stop breaking when 9.3 lands, set ROCQ_IMAGE=docker.io/rocq/rocq-prover:9.2 in the workflow.

I verified the script under shellcheck and exercised the container-dispatch, native, failure, and cleanup paths with a stubbed rocq; I couldn't pull the real image from this sandbox, so the one thing untested end-to-end is the actual rocq compile invocation.
